processing: As with other Mengku raw pu-erh, the leaf is pan-fired, rolled and sun-dried, then pressed or kept loose, with no ripening pile.
harvest_season: Spring is the most valued picking, as is usual across Mengku. Villagers still return to the old gardens to pick each season.
appearance_dry: Long dark green strips of large leaf, typical of Mengku raw tea.
appearance_wet: Thick yellow-green large leaves that open fully.
taste_profile: Little is recorded about this village's own taste. As with other Mengku raw teas, expect a full body, some bitterness and a returning sweetness.

brewing.notes: Hot water and short early steeps, as with other young Mengku raw teas.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year as mao cha or pressed cakes, in small quantities since output is low. Price accounts disagree: one list gives 2,100 to 2,300 yuan a kilo for old trees, while another account compares it with the old village. Pure old-garden Nuowu is hard to find, so treat a confident label with some doubt.
description:
Nuowu is one of the five settlements of the Bingdao village committee in Mengku. Unlike the old village, Nanpo and Dijie it lies on the eastern side of the Nanmeng River, together with Bawai.

The method is the normal one for raw pu-erh here. The trees in its old garden are said to be similar in size to those at Bawai's old village and probably of a similar age.

Flavour notes specific to Nuowu are scarce. As with other Mengku raw teas, expect a full body, some bitterness and returning sweetness, and brew with hot water and short steeps.

Output is small. Its name is known within Mengku, and pure tea from the old village can be harder to buy than pure Bingdao old-village tea, so ask for the year, the maker and the garden.
history: Nuowu's old village had 35 households in 2003. In 2004 the county moved the whole village to the highway below the mountain and funded a new settlement, Nuowu Xinzhai. The Lahu residents still go back to pick from the fifty or sixty acres of old gardens during the season.
